name: Tirzepatide

track.title: Lab & animal

what.text: Tirzepatide is a single man-made peptide that switches on two gut-hormone receptors: GIP and GLP-1. It has a fatty chain that binds to a blood protein called albumin, which makes it last longer in the body.

GLP-1 helps control appetite and how much food people eat. The label says studies outside people suggest GIP may add to that effect. In animal studies, tirzepatide reached and switched on nerve cells in brain areas that control appetite. Those findings come from animals.
The FDA-approved brands are Mounjaro and Zepbound, both made by Eli Lilly and given by injection under the skin.
The trials below tested tirzepatide by itself. None tested tirzepatide combined with vitamin B12 or glycine.

research.text: Tirzepatide has been tested in large randomized Phase 3 trials paid for by its maker, Eli Lilly. Five are listed below exactly as they were run: one in type 2 diabetes, one for weight, two for sleep apnea (reported together), and one on heart outcomes.

research.title: SURPASS-2: tirzepatide vs semaglutide in type 2 diabetes

facts.v: Phase 3, randomized, open-label (people knew which drug they got). No placebo; the comparison was semaglutide.
1,879 adults with type 2 diabetes. Average age 56.6, average weight 93.7 kg.
weekly tirzepatide (5, 10 or 15 mg) or weekly semaglutide 1 mg
change in HbA1c, a three-month blood sugar measure

research.found: HbA1c fell 2.01 to 2.30 percentage points on the three tirzepatide doses and 1.86 points on semaglutide. Tirzepatide met the trial's tests for being no worse and for being better. Nausea was reported by 17 to 22% on tirzepatide and 18% on semaglutide. Serious adverse events were reported in 5 to 7% on tirzepatide and 3% on semaglutide. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03987919.

src.label: Frías et al., SURPASS-2, N Engl J Med 2021

research.title: SURMOUNT-1: weight in adults without diabetes

facts.v: 2,539 adults with a BMI of 30 or more, or 27 or more with at least one weight-related complication. People with diabetes were excluded. Average starting weight 104.8 kg.
weekly tirzepatide (5, 10 or 15 mg) or placebo, with a 20-week dose increase at the start
percent change in body weight, and how many people lost at least 5%

research.found: Average weight changed by -15.0%, -19.5% and -20.9% on the three tirzepatide doses and -3.1% on placebo. 85 to 91% on tirzepatide and 35% on placebo lost at least 5%. Side effects were mostly stomach and bowel effects, mainly while the dose was being raised. 4.3 to 7.1% on tirzepatide and 2.6% on placebo stopped because of side effects. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04184622.

src.label: Jastreboff et al., SURMOUNT-1, N Engl J Med 2022

research.title: SURMOUNT-OSA: obstructive sleep apnea and obesity

facts.v: two Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials. Trial 1 enrolled people not using a CPAP-type breathing machine; trial 2 enrolled people using one.
adults with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea and obesity. The registry lists 469 people enrolled in total.
the highest tolerated weekly tirzepatide dose (10 or 15 mg) or placebo
change in the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), the number of breathing pauses and shallow breaths per hour of sleep

research.found: Starting AHI averaged about 50 events per hour. In trial 1, AHI fell by 25.3 events per hour on tirzepatide and 5.3 on placebo. In trial 2, it fell by 29.3 on tirzepatide and 5.5 on placebo. The most frequent side effects were stomach and bowel effects, mostly mild to moderate. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05412004.

src.label: Malhotra et al., SURMOUNT-OSA, N Engl J Med 2024

research.title: SURPASS-CVOT: heart outcomes vs dulaglutide in type 2 diabetes

facts.v: randomized, double-blind. No placebo; the comparison was dulaglutide, another GLP-1 medicine. Built first to show tirzepatide was no worse.
13,299 adults with type 2 diabetes and artery disease were randomized; 13,165 were analyzed. Average age 64.1; 29.0% were women.
weekly tirzepatide (up to 15 mg) or weekly dulaglutide 1.5 mg
heart-related death, heart attack or stroke, counted together

research.found: The combined outcome happened in 12.2% on tirzepatide and 13.1% on dulaglutide (hazard ratio 0.92). Tirzepatide met the test for being no worse, but not the test for being better. Stomach and bowel side effects were more common on tirzepatide. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04255433.

src.label: Nicholls et al., SURPASS-CVOT, N Engl J Med 2025

research.text: In a two-year study, rats given tirzepatide under the skin developed more thyroid C-cell tumors at exposures similar to those in people. A six-month study in a strain of mice bred for cancer testing found no tumors. It is not known whether the rat finding applies to humans. Tirzepatide did not damage DNA in a rat test.

us.text: Tirzepatide is FDA approved under two brand names: Mounjaro and Zepbound. Compounded tirzepatide is not FDA approved. FDA says the tirzepatide shortage ended in December 2024. As of October 31, 2026.
Compounded drugs are not FDA approved. FDA does not review their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold.

src.label: FDA, Compounding and the FDA: Q&A

items.text: approved, with diet and exercise, to improve blood sugar control in adults and children 10 and older with type 2 diabetes. In August 2026 the label added a use: lowering the risk of major heart events in adults with type 2 diabetes at high risk.

approved, with a reduced-calorie diet and more physical activity, for long-term weight reduction in adults with obesity, or adults with overweight and at least one weight-related condition. Also approved to treat moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity.
in the US, Mounjaro is approved for type 2 diabetes and heart risk, not for weight management. Using Mounjaro for weight loss is off-label.

tirzepatide injections were on FDA's shortage list from 2022. FDA said the shortage was resolved on October 2, 2024, re-evaluated that during a lawsuit, and decided again on December 19, 2024 that it was resolved.

src.label: FDA: Clarifies policies for compounders as GLP-1 supply stabilizes

items.text: pharmacies may not regularly compound drugs that are essentially copies of a commercially available drug, unless a prescriber documents a significant difference for an individual patient. FDA's test also covers a compounded drug that combines the active ingredients of two or more available products in similar strengths by the same route. FDA's worked example named semaglutide with vitamin B12; it did not give a tirzepatide example.

src.label: FDA: Clarifies policies for compounders as GLP-1 supply stabilizes

items.text: on March 3, 2026, FDA announced 30 warning letters to telehealth companies over false or misleading claims about compounded GLP-1s, including claims that they are the same as approved drugs. A June 8, 2026 letter cited a site claiming compounded tirzepatide "offers the same results" as Mounjaro and that its pharmacies were "FDA approved". FDA said compounded drugs are not FDA approved and that pharmacies have no FDA-approved designation.

items.text: FDA is aware of fraudulent compounded tirzepatide whose labels name pharmacies that do not exist or that did not make it.

world.lead: Tirzepatide is an approved, prescription-only medicine in the US, the EU and the UK, and its brands are listed in Canada's drug database. Outside the US, Mounjaro itself is approved for weight management. Australia's record could not be reached. It is not prohibited in sport.

after.title: Sport
after.text: USADA says GLP-1 medicines, including tirzepatide, are not prohibited in sport and need no therapeutic use exemption. USADA says semaglutide and tirzepatide are in WADA's 2027 Monitoring Program, which takes effect January 1, 2027. Monitored substances are not prohibited; labs test for them so WADA can study their use. We could not open WADA's own list to confirm.

side.text: Both tirzepatide labels have a boxed warning, FDA's strongest kind, about thyroid C-cell tumors. The most common side effects are stomach and bowel effects. The labels list other serious risks, below.

items.text: in rats, tirzepatide caused thyroid C-cell tumors. It is not known if it causes these tumors, including medullary thyroid cancer, in people. People with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer, or with MEN 2 syndrome, must not use it. Warning signs include a lump in the neck, trouble swallowing, shortness of breath and lasting hoarseness.

in two Zepbound weight trials, severe stomach and bowel side effects were reported in 1.7% to 3.1% on tirzepatide, depending on dose, and 1% on placebo. After approval, reports have included bowel blockage and severe constipation.
inflammation of the pancreas, including bleeding and tissue-death forms that sometimes caused death, has been reported after approval.

src.label: MHRA: GLP-1 medicines for weight loss and diabetes, what you need to know

items.text: in the two weight trials, gallbladder inflammation was reported in 0.7% on tirzepatide and 0.2% on placebo.
both labels warn of sudden kidney injury from dehydration, for example after vomiting or diarrhea.
in a weight trial in people with type 2 diabetes, low blood sugar was reported in 4.2% on tirzepatide and 1.3% on placebo. The risk was higher in people also taking a sulfonylurea.
serious reactions, including anaphylaxis and swelling under the skin (angioedema), have been reported.
fast improvement in blood sugar has been linked to temporary worsening of diabetic retinopathy.
tirzepatide slows stomach emptying. There are rare reports with GLP-1 medicines of stomach contents entering the lungs during general anesthesia or deep sedation.
the labels say tirzepatide may make birth control pills work less well, because it slows stomach emptying, mostly after the first dose and after each dose increase.
nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation, belly pain, indigestion, injection site reactions, tiredness, allergic reactions, burping, hair loss and acid reflux (Zepbound label).

FDA has reports of side effects in people given compounded tirzepatide at doses beyond the approved label, and one report of injection-site redness, swelling and pain with a product labelled with a pharmacy that did not make it.

Australia's TGA website could not be reached, so tirzepatide's status there (ARTG listing and the rules on compounding) is not shown.
WADA's website blocked access, so the 2026 and 2027 Prohibited Lists could not be opened; the sport status is taken from USADA.
The approved uses of Mounjaro and Zepbound in Canada were not checked; only their listing in the Drug Product Database was. Health Canada's status record for Mounjaro could not be retrieved.
The year Zepbound's sleep apnea use was added was not confirmed from an FDA approval letter, so it is not given.
Whether the EU authorises a separate Zepbound brand was not checked.
surprises: Compounding is often explained by the shortage, but FDA declared the tirzepatide shortage resolved on December 19, 2024, and says tirzepatide is not on its shortage list.
Some sellers say compounded tirzepatide gives "the same results" as Mounjaro or comes from "FDA approved" pharmacies; FDA's warning letters call these claims false or misleading.

Mounjaro is often called a weight-loss drug, but its US label covers type 2 diabetes and heart risk only; the US weight brand is Zepbound. In the EU and UK, Mounjaro itself is approved for weight management.
The Zepbound label removed its warning section on suicidal behavior and ideation in February 2026.
